compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`rapt-dreadable-dromedary` (`aefe-614a-2631-4117`) replaced the bare `os.path.isdir` init
predicate with the shared `store_is_usable` (`.git` present AND `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`
resolves) at the LIBRARY/MCP read chokepoint (`_reads._tracker`) and at the low-level write
gate (`event_prepare._ensure_initialized`). That was the approved scope.

The CLI read path was explicitly left out of that scope and still carries the original
predicate at two sites:

- `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:340`
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:384`

Both are `if not os.path.isdir(tracker):`. So a tracker directory that EXISTS but is not a
usable store — no `.git` (the shape observed on the deployed MCP server), or a `.git` whose HEAD
does not resolve because a clone is still in flight — passes the CLI guard exactly as it used to
pass the library one, and the CLI read reports an empty store rather than
`store_uninitialized`.

The result is a NEW surface disagreement introduced by the parent fix: for the same broken
store, `rebar.list_tickets()` (library / MCP) now raises `store_uninitialized` while `rebar list`
(CLI) still prints an empty result. Before the parent fix the two agreed (both wrong); they now
disagree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both `reads_cli.py` sites use the shared `rebar._store.store_usability.store_is_usable`
      predicate rather than a bare `os.path.isdir`.
- [ ] A CLI read against a present-but-unusable store (no `.git`) reports the uninitialized
      store, not an empty result.
- [ ] A CLI read against a mid-clone store (`.git` present, HEAD unresolvable) does the same.
- [ ] A CLI read against an existing, empty, INITIALIZED store still reports an empty result
      (the no-regression half — the discriminator must not become emptiness).
- [ ] A CLI read against a valid clone with a resolvable HEAD but NO `.env-id` still succeeds
      and returns its tickets (anchored on a seeded ticket, so a vacuous empty result cannot
      pass), matching the library asymmetry: reads do not require `.env-id`, writes do.
- [ ] Regression: reverting either site to a bare `os.path.isdir` returns the broken/mid-clone
      cases to RED (defect-seeded mutation check).

## Notes

Found during the parent fix's parity sweep; recorded there as out-of-approved-scope rather than
folded in, to keep that change reviewable.
compiled_state.title: CLI read path still gates on bare os.path.isdir, so a present-but-unusable store reads empty there
